title: Edge count of the Harary graph
statement: Let $m$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $n \ge 1$ and $m < n$, and let $H_{m,n}$ be the Harary graph on the $n$ vertices $\bbz/n\bbz$. Then $H_{m,n}$ has exactly $\lceil mn/2 \rceil$ edges (equivalently, $\lfloor (mn+1)/2 \rfloor$).
replaced:
Edge count / optimality: \texttt{H\_\{m,n\}} has \texttt{$\lceil$mn/2$\rceil$} edges.

It is easy to see that $\varepsilon(H_{m,n}) = \{mn/2\}$. Thus, by theorem 3.3, \[f(m,
n) \le \{mn/2\} \qquad (3.2)\] It now follows from (3.1) and (3.2) that \[f(m, n) =
\{mn/2\}\] and that $H_{m,n}$ is an $m$-connected graph on $n$ vertices with as few
edges as possible. We note that since, for any graph $G$, $\kappa \le \kappa'$ (theorem
3.1), $H_{m,n}$ is also $m$-edge-connected. Thus, denoting by $g(m, n)$ the least
possible number of edges in an $m$-edge-connected graph on $n$ vertices, we have, for $1
< m < n$ \[g(m, n) = \{mn/2\} \qquad (3.3)\]
